title: Java homework series evaluated for ChatGPT exposure
summary: Students independently complete 22 auto-graded Java homework exercises in a first-semester programming course. ChatGPT was tested offline on the same briefs, motivating assessment features such as template TODOs, non-textual requirements, hidden and dynamic tests, documentation, and code-quality checks.

sources.title: Recommendations to Create Programming Exercises to Overcome ChatGPT
sources.evidence_quote: 22 exercises from an introductory programming course

assessment.summary: Solve 22 Java programming homework exercises in Artemis.
student_actions: Submit code to the automated assessment platform.

student_role.description: The instructor evaluated ChatGPT on the assignments; student AI permission was not reported.

grading.method: Artemis auto-grading; the homework series formed the practical course component.

related_assessments.description: Distinct assessment reported in the same source.

provenance.extraction_method: Full PDF read from pdftotext output.

reported_results: Sixty-five students completed the 12-week course; ChatGPT averaged 55% on one-shot attempts across the 22 exercises.
